description: We are a team of four currently, looking for experienced Java developers, experience with database/SQL knowledge, and hope to create a program that will help push astronauts to be safe in relation to space travel.
summary:
The Goal of this program is for astronauts to use this program daily to monitor their physical health, find red flags in their routine, and then act accordingly, either by making chances themselves or talking to a medical officer.

The program begins by asking the user for basic information. Once these questions are filled, a menu will drop down asking the user to select from the following options:

Vision Questionnaire, Red Blood Cell Amount, Bone Density, Blood Lab, Muscle Atrophy test,  and Radiation Exposure.

Each option chosen has a different list of questions to be answered, in which the user (in some, not ALL) may need the results of tests outside of program to enter in. Once these values are entered, they will be compared to the expected average person, if the entered values fall outside this range, the program will print that it sees this issue, otherwise anything within the expected ranges will not cause any red flags. The user is now expected to use the program in order to alert a medical officer of their results, and from there the trained professional will decide the best course of action.
details:
The Goal of this program is for astronauts to use this program daily to monitor their physical health, find red flags in their routine, and then act accordingly.
To do this, we have the user have all the relevant data taken via ultrasounds, blood testing, etc, and when asked, input them into this program
From there the program will compare the inputted data to the average expected amount and if the inputted value is outside of this scope, the program responds accordingly.

We created this program using the software language Python, and used Thonny to write the entire script using our own laptops.
The intended impact is a more stable and safe environment for astronauts. With this program, their health is documented very frequently and as such, can detect irregularities extremely quickly, quite possibly preventing avoidable danger.

My team had to search through all relevant factors/data that zero gravity would have on a persons health, once enough data was collected, we had to research the safe and unsafe levels in order to develop the acceptable ranges.
